## Rule

ARC-GEN task_662c240a: input is three stacked 3x3 blocks. Exactly one block is asymmetric under main-diagonal transpose; output is that asymmetric 3x3 block.

## Algorithm sketch

Split rows 0:3, 3:6, 6:9 at cols 0:3; choose the block whose color-index matrix differs from its transpose; pad the selected 3x3 one-hot block back to the 30x30 NeuroGolf canvas.

## Cost analysis

Current staged best (2026-06-21) keeps the skip-block-0 selector and beats Aditya/team-best 495 by comparing the two checksum scalars before `Split`. The row selector only needs block 1 and block 2 checks; if both are symmetric, the exactly-one-asymmetric invariant selects block 0 by elimination. Negative begin/end Conv pads crop the checksum Conv to rows 3 and 6, reducing `checks` from [1,1,3,1] to `checks12` [1,1,2,1]. The 2026-06-21 rewrite changes `Equal(check)->Split` so the split outputs are BOOL flags, not F32 scalar checks, lowering cost from 487 to 481.

Dominant charges: `selected` [1,9,3,3] F32 = 324 B, `checks12` = 8 B, `sym12_full` = 2 B, `b1_eq0`/`b2_eq0` = 2 B total, plus 107 params led by `w_checksum` = 90. No absolute floor claimed: within the current checksum+dynamic-Slice output family, the hard remaining charge is the F32 selected one-hot block. A different output construction would need to avoid full-canvas color-index materialization and the 324 B selected crop to beat 481 meaningfully.

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._
- 2026-06-11 [worker-3]: team-best cleanup-only route has an unused `false_bool` initializer but saves only 1 param; not worth staging alone. `ReduceMax(BOOL)` variant is valid/correct at cost 1836, but `ReduceMin(BOOL)+Not` is 24 B cheaper. Direct U8 one-hot symmetry test materializes 90 B transpose/equality planes per block and loses to Conv labels. Full 9x3 shared-label reshape route adds reshape/slice tensors and did not beat independent 3x3 blocks.
- 2026-06-20 [w16]: full color-index plane + Equal-tail one-hot is not a cheap sub-495 path because a 1x1 color-index Conv over the 30x30 input materializes a 3600 B intermediate unless preceded by an even costlier crop. Channel-cropping to remove ch0 before the checksum also loses; the F32 crop costs more than the 10 checksum params it saves.
- 2026-06-21 [worker-146]: technique #46 Einsum detector was priced but not staged. Legal direct-input forms need color plus row/column operands for both the block-row windows and local 3-column coordinates, replacing the 90-param checksum Conv with larger operand banks while leaving the 324 B selected block unchanged. BOOL output tail also loses because the F32 `Slice(input)` selected crop is still charged before any Cast/Pad.
- 2026-06-24 [w7 beta_p29]: **#46 repeated-subscript diagonal trace route is mathematically WRONG for this rule, not just a pricing tie.** The rule is *transpose*-asymmetry (block differs from its main-diagonal transpose: `c[i,j] != c[j,i]`). The prompt's suggested signal — "diagonal vs anti-diagonal trace gap" via `Einsum('hh')` repeated-subscript — measures a different property. Counterexample: `c=[[0,1,0],[0,0,0],[0,0,0]]` is transpose-asymmetric yet has main-diag trace 0 AND anti-diag trace 0, so a pure diagonal-read Einsum scores it symmetric and MISSES it (hidden 0). Any correct off-diagonal comparison needs `c[i,j]` vs `c[j,i]`, which requires a Transpose plane (prompt forbids it) or the existing antisymmetric checksum Conv. The current 481 graph's 90-param antisymmetric `w_checksum` Conv IS the cheapest correct off-diagonal asymmetry detector; #46 cannot replace it. NO CANDIDATE. Floor stands at 481 (memory 374 + params 107; `selected [1,9,3,3] F32` = 324 B is the unavoidable output crop).
